html:
Pope Francis, born Jorge Mario Bergoglio in Buenos Aires, Argentina, was head of the Catholic Church from 2013 until his death in 2025. He was the first pope from the Americas and the first from the Jesuit order.

The son of Italian immigrants, he joined the Jesuits in 1958 and led them in Argentina during the years of military rule. He became archbishop of Buenos Aires in 1998 and a cardinal in 2001. He was known for taking the bus and living simply.

After Benedict XVI resigned, the cardinals elected him in March 2013. He took the name Francis after Francis of Assisi, the saint of the poor.

  • He called for a "poor church for the poor" and spoke often for migrants.
  • His letter Laudato si' (2015) asked the world to act on climate change.
  • He took a gentler tone on gay people and divorced Catholics, which drew both praise and opposition inside the church.
  • He made the Salvadoran archbishop Óscar Romero, a hero of liberation theology, a saint.

He died on Easter Monday 2025. The American Leo XIV succeeded him.
sum: Pope Francis, born Jorge Mario Bergoglio in Buenos Aires, Argentina, was head of the Catholic Church from 2013 until his death in 2025. He was the first pope from the Americas and the first from the Jesuit order.
